recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future ElementDefinition.condition omissions should be handled through specific resource/profile trackers, matching the FHIR-I disposition, rather than reopening broad automatic inference work.
issue_request: FHIR-24860 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking to reduce inconsistent base-resource use of ElementDefinition.condition. The approved disposition rejected automatic parsing of arbitrary FHIRPath expressions and instead called for explicit attention to invariants during QA review, with concrete model misses handled by specific trackers.
initial_application: Commit 55512f8e09be7228efab289f8bf660242d29654d, "clean up invariants and conditions ( FHIR-24860)", already applied source metadata cleanup across many active StructureDefinition sources. It added pat-1 condition references to Patient.contact.name, Patient.contact.telecom, and Patient.contact.address, completing the original Patient example alongside the existing organization reference.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-03-23 confirm the 12-0-0 decision. The later Patient-specific follow-up FHIR-37865 was resolved Retracted, and current Patient source contains pat-1 condition metadata on all four affected children. source/fhir.ini lists Patient as an active resource, and documentation.html links validation.html, whose validation overview includes invariant checking; no separate active source page for a ballot-review checklist was found that would justify a targeted current-build edit.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current build sources already reflect the implemented cleanup for the concrete inconsistency that motivated the issue, and adding redundant implementer-facing prose would not improve the specification's conformance meaning.
